order: Fix continuous-integration failures on macOS and Windows that appeared following the structural sweep guard change. Git records canonical worktree paths, but a live checkout's own handle may be spelled through a symlink or a short alias path, so a lexical comparison inside the sweep's live-set exemption misses the match and the sweep deletes a live checkout mid-verification. The path-normalization function must look up real paths first, and must fall back to a lexical comparison only for paths that are already gone — never for a path still on disk. Pin a regression using an aliased temporary-root reproducer, such as a junction or symlink, that must fail on every platform without the fix and must pass cleanly once the fix lands, skipping only where links cannot be created. Keep the fix scoped to the normalization function and the live-set comparison only; do not touch the sweep's other classification logic, which must remain unchanged.
claims: The live-set exemption's path comparison now looks up real paths, falling back lexically only for paths already gone, which fixes the macOS and Windows continuous-integration failures caused by a canonical-versus-aliased path mismatch. A regression was pinned using an aliased temporary-root reproducer, built from a junction or symlink, that fails on every platform without the fix; the diff stat shows 25 lines added to the verifier test suite and 11 to the checkout module, with no other files touched.
